collateral.note: Testnet collateral is tUSDC at 6 decimals. USDso (18 decimals) is MAINNET ONLY. Derive scale from decimals(), never a literal.

SeasonPrizePool.note: Escrows a season prize pool. Allocations freeze at finalize(); each winner claims once; surplus withdrawal is bounded by funded - allocated so an unclaimed prize can never be swept.

readsConfirmed: swipeDigest(...) returns a valid EIP-712 digest

liveDuel.note: Created on live Shannon testnet to prove the state machine end to end.

steps: joinDuel from a second wallet — success
revealDeck — success; contract recomputed the commitment
recordSwipe x2 — both players signed EIP-712 off-chain, relayer paid gas

result.note: Scores match the economics exactly: backing UP at 0.40 and winning redeems 1.00 for +0.60; the losing side forfeits its 0.40 premium.

fullLifecycle.proves: Neither player sent a transaction — the relayer submitted both swipes. That is the core UX claim of the Somnia migration, verified on chain.

gasNotes.deployEstimateVsActual: Foundry estimated 3,394,836 gas; the deploy actually needed 38,853,709 (11x). Somnia prices contract-code state creation far above Ethereum.
gasNotes.failureMode: An under-limit deploy mines with status 0 and burns the ENTIRE limit, while eth_call simulation still succeeds — so simulation cannot catch it. Three deploys failed this way (3.4M, 12M, 8M) before 60M succeeded.
gasNotes.guidance: Set a deploy gas limit far above the estimate. Unused gas is refunded on success, so over-provisioning is cheap and under-provisioning is not.
gasNotes.sizeScaling: Gas tracks contract code size closely: 11,440-byte runtime needed 38.85M, 4,401-byte runtime needed 15.57M. Note the gas LIMIT is also balance-checked upfront (limit x gasPrice must be affordable), so an over-large limit can be rejected as 'insufficient balance' even when the tx would only spend a fraction of it.
